stage1.impression: A symmetrical, stage-like niche with two speakers glowing salmon-pink like neon signs, flanked by flat red panels, with smooth coral tub chairs and a white ping-pong-ball lamp in the foreground. The end-grain wall is a visibly repeating grid texture, the carpet and chairs are smooth CG surfaces, and the sides and ceiling fall into empty near-black. It reads as a game or home-cinema showroom render, not a photograph of a specific place, and a design magazine would not run it as one.

blocking_9: Speaker acrylic frames must stop reading as pink neon: speaker region clip_pct < 1 with the tint still reading as red cast acrylic, not as signage
End-grain block wall must read as real end grain (growth rings, varied block tone, irregular joints) with no visible texture repeat; wall region lum_range >= 30
Velvet chairs must show nap and a sheen falloff at their rolled edges instead of smooth plastic-looking colour
The Orb lamp must read as smoked acrylic glowing from within, not as a matte white ball lit from above
Pools of light on the carpet and between the chairs, with dark falloff between them: floor falloff, not a flat plane (current range 21)
The frame edges (left and right walls, ceiling and beams) need readable detail, not flat near-black at lum ~13 to 16 with a range of 5
A sign of life in the zone: a glass on the table, a record or sleeve, a coat or a bag on a chair
A full-resolution render without denoiser smear on the wall, the carpet and the speaker internals

defects.what: End-grain wall is a uniform square grid with the same horizontal wood-grain stripe repeating: tiled texture, flat (lum_range 17 in 300-420 x 80-300)
Left speaker's acrylic frame blows to pink-white, clip 7.7% in the frame region, so it reads as neon tube or signage
Right speaker same: pink-white neon frame, clip 4.4% in the speaker region
Top horn module (resin horn/cover zone) is a smeared red blur with no edge definition, likely denoiser
Tub chairs are smooth, evenly coloured coral surfaces with no velvet nap, pile direction or sheen at the rolled edges: reads as plastic
Foreground chair the same: smooth CG velvet, soft blurred top edge
Orb lamp reads as a matte grey-white ball (RGB 138/106/95), no smoke tint, no internal glow, no liner visible
Hexagonal table top is hot (p95 192) and flat; oak grain not legible
Carpet is a uniform flat plane (lum 42 to 49 across its depth): no pools of light, no wool texture
Left edge dead flat dark (lum_median 15.6, range 5.2): empty, no wall or detail
Right edge similarly empty and dark
Ceiling band empty (lum_median 12.8): no Douglas fir beams or concrete readable
Altar spot makes a hard-edged hotspot cone on the red panel above each speaker, read as a stage wash
Oak plinths read as flat brown boxes with no grain or edge highlight
Everything is red: chairs, panels, speakers and walls all warm red, so the speaker is not the one saturated note; denoiser smear throughout at this proof scale

changes.problem: The speakers' acrylic frames are blown to pink-white and read as neon signage rather than tinted cast acrylic.

evidence.measured: lum_p95 199.9, clip_pct 7.66, RGB median 156/82/79; whole speaker region clip 4.0% (left), 4.4% (right)

change.setting: lamps on each Ember speaker (4 x area)
change.to: 6.0 W/m2 at the target, 2900 K, and raise the altar spots from 40.0 W to 55.0 W so the cabinets are lit from outside and the acrylic shows edge glow rather than a lit-from-within tube

changes.expected: Frames keep a deep red tint with only thin bright polished edges; the woofer and batts stay legible; the speaker reads as a translucent object, not a sign.

changes.problem: The end-grain block wall is a visibly tiling grid texture with flat tone, the single biggest 'render' tell.

evidence.measured: lum_range 17.1, lum_median 44.7; the same horizontal grain stripe repeats every block row

change.setting: end-grain block finish (material finish of the niche lining)
change.from: one wood-grain map tiled across a regular grid
change.to: end-grain texture (growth rings and radial checks) per block, with random per-block rotation, offset and a +/-15% value and hue jitter; joints darker and slightly irregular (1 to 2 mm); roughness 0.7 with a slight oil sheen

changes.expected: The wall reads as hand-laid end-grain blocks with variation, no repeat visible at 1:1, and enough tonal variation to carry the warm light.

changes.problem: The Orb lamp on the table reads as a matte white ball lit from above, not a smoked acrylic lamp glowing from within, and the table under it is hot.

evidence.measured: RGB median 138/106/95, lum_median 112; table top 240-345 x 410-470 p95 191.6

change.setting: each Orb (lamp W and liner glow) and the Domes' downlights
change.from: Orb 6.0 W, glow 0.6; Domes' downlights 320.0 W
change.to: Orb 10.0 W, glow 1.6; Domes' downlights 200.0 W, so the Orb is the table's key light and the downlights no longer flatten it

changes.expected: The Orb shows a dark smoked shell with a warm glowing frosted core; a soft pool of amber light on the oak top; the table no longer hot-spotted.

changes.problem: The velvet tub chairs read as smooth, evenly coloured plastic shells, not velvet.

evidence.measured: lum_range 73.5, but smooth gradient with no texture; colour RGB 106/34/34 (delta E 3.7 to oxblood, so colour is fine; surface is wrong)

change.setting: velvet finish on the tub chairs
change.to: velvet: sheen 1.0 with sheen tint 0.5, roughness 0.9, a fine pile normal map, and a slight darkening of the face-on areas so the rolled rims catch a lighter grazing sheen

changes.expected: The rims of the chairs glow lighter where the light grazes them and the faces go deeper oxblood, the signature of velvet; the zone reads as a rich colour, not as coral plastic.

changes.problem: The frame's edges and ceiling are empty near-black, so the room has no context (no concrete, fir beams or steel), and the zone floats like a stage set.

change.setting: a new low wall-grazing source, or the Domes' downlights re-aimed, plus haze
change.from: no light on the side walls or the beams; haze 0.012 per m
change.to: two 15 W 2700 K grazers washing the side walls and one 20 W uplight onto the nearest Douglas fir beam; haze 0.025 per m so the altar spots show soft beams

changes.expected: Board-formed concrete or fir faintly readable at the frame's edges and a beam visible overhead, holding shadow detail while staying dark.

changes.problem: The carpet is a flat even plane with no pools of light and dark between the seats.

evidence.measured: falloff along y 41.6 to 49.4 to 44.8; lum_range 21.5

change.setting: the Domes' downlights' cone, and the altar spots' aim
change.to: cone 28 deg, aimed on the tables and chair seats; tilt the altar spots so their lower edge spills a pool on the carpet in front of each plinth

changes.expected: Distinct pools of light on the tables and the carpet before each speaker with darker carpet between, giving depth and the 'pools of light' look.

changes.problem: There is no sign of life in the listening zone; it reads as an empty showroom.

evidence.measured: only the Orb and an indistinct dark object on the table

change.from: props only at the counter (glasses, coat, candles) and none in the zone
change.to: a rocks glass with whisky and a coaster beside the Orb, a record sleeve leaning on the right chair's arm, a folded jacket over the left chair's back

changes.expected: The zone reads as occupied a moment ago, with small highlights in the glass picking up the Orb.

changes.problem: Detail is smeared by the denoiser at proof scale (horn module, wall, carpet), and the altar spots make hard stage-like cones on the red panels.

evidence.measured: falloff along y 28.9 / 32.0 / 44.5 / 39.6 / 46.5 / 33.5 / 57.4 / 33.6: banded hot and cold bands instead of a smooth fall-off

change.from: proof at scale 0.3, denoise on; altar spots cone 40.0 deg with a hard edge
change.to: judge at full 2400 x 1600 with samples 512; altar spots given a soft edge (blend 0.6) and cone 50 deg so the panel shows a smooth fall-off from top to bottom

changes.expected: Crisp edges on the speaker internals and the blocks; a smooth graded pool on each panel rather than a theatrical cone.

out_of_scope.request: Make the speaker the only saturated colour in the frame
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes the oxblood zone (chairs, carpet, limewashed walls, red panels) as the design, so the speaker cannot be the only saturated note; the light changes above help it stand out by brightness and translucency instead.

out_of_scope.request: Change the speakers' pink-red frames or their translucent tint
out_of_scope.why: EARF's product (shape, colour, parts) is fixed; only its lighting can change.

out_of_scope.request: Break the dead-centre symmetric composition with a different niche layout
out_of_scope.why: The altar and niche layout are fixed design; a camera move off-axis (for example 0.6 m to the left with a 40 mm lens) is allowed but moves every region, so it is offered here without a pixel test.
